# Terrain effects

Used in [Movement](/rules/40-movement), [Stacking, zones of control and reserve](/rules/50-stacking-and-zoc), [Combat](/rules/60-combat).

::: tip Errata applied
- **E-031** — Terrain Effects Chart: footnote 4 (level-three fortifications) belongs to Major City, not Swamp; a track does not cost 1 CP, it halves the cost of the hex's terrain (footnote 8 is right, the printed '1' is not)
:::

## Notes

- Anti-armour column: the L shifts on ridge, up/down slope and down escarpment apply where fire is allowed. Case 14.34 bans anti-armour fire, by the assaulting points, across a ridge with no road or track, down a slope with no road or track, and down an escarpment with no track; 'prohibited' on up-escarpment is unconditional. Up and down are the phasing assault's direction
- Terrain Effects Chart (SPI 8.37): hex terrain, hexside features (cp is additive, the chart's '+'), fortification levels and minefields. Column shifts are signed: negative = L (columns to the left, favouring the defender), positive = R. 'gravel' here is the same terrain as 'sand-gravel' on the Construction Chart (construction.json)
- Printed as in 1979: track costs 1 CP with footnote 8 and footnote 4 sits on Swamp. SPI's September 1979 errata (E-031) moves footnote 4 to Major City and says tracks do not cost 1 CP — they halve the hex terrain's cost (footnote 8 is correct, the '1' is not); the overlay data/errata/E-031.json applies both
- The chart is on a page of the rulebook (jp2 69), not the shared chart sheet. Transcribed from the archive.org scan and cross-checked cell by cell against the community's OCR-converted scan of the 1979 rulebook (scan:discord:CampaignNorthAfrica - converted.pdf:p70): 0 of 27 rows differ. Clay Stone's errata-integrated Land rules PDF prints 'see Charts and Tables' with the two errata sentences in place of the chart

## Footnotes

1. a garrison unit in its assigned hex takes no stacking space; anti-aircraft units take none in a major city (any number), at an airfield (up to three) or at a landing strip (one)
2. enterable and leavable, by track only, for light trucks, recce and motorcycle infantry — no other vehicle; nothing motorised fights into or out of a salt marsh (8.44)
3. light trucks, motorcycle recce and motorcycle infantry may not enter, even by track
4. Alexandria and Cairo hexes are level-three fortifications; every other one is level two
5. Commonwealth units may be able to use rail movement (8.7)
6. negates all hexside entry costs and breakdown values
7. counts only what is actually on the road or track: the units and truck points using it in that hex at that moment
8. halves all terrain entry costs and all hex and hexside breakdown values, except the CP and breakdown of a vehicle going down an escarpment
9. motorised units and trucks may cross only on a track
10. in a rainstorm may be crossed only where a road or railroad (treated as a road) crosses the hexside, at +2 CP
11. may be crossed only where a road or railroad crosses the hexside; a motorised unit then pays no CP or breakdown for it
12. armour targets get the defensive benefit only in a major city hex
13. engineers cut the entry cost (26.2); assaulting forces standing in an enemy minefield give the non-phasing side L1 on anti-armour and close assault unless it already has them from a friendly minefield
